messages:
alicia: Heads-up — I'm seeing repeated asks from PMs about showing per-model token burn inside per-route views. They want to compare model variants for the same route without switching pages.
ben: +1 from eng. We have the data but exposing it will change the routing UX. Do we show per-model rows, a dropdown, or inline sparkbars?
sam: I sketched a mock: route page stays the same, add a collapsible 'models' pane that lists eligible model variants with cost/latency columns. Click expands to show recent samples and token burn breakdown.
maria: Concern: saved queries currently serialize a single model pin per-route. If we show multiple variants, savedquery schema needs extension or we'll confuse users.
alicia: Right. Two separate problems: console UX (how to display multiple model-level metrics) and savedquery contract (what gets persisted/rolled out). We should split decisions.
ben: For UX: prefer a minimal approach first — show a compact 'model selector' pill with a small sparkbar + cost delta. Detailed table in a flyout. Keeps route-level view readable.
sam: Implement notes: backend already emits model_id + telemetry per-request. We can aggregate per-route/per-model. Need API change to return models[] in the route telemetry endpoint instead of flat metrics.
maria: On savedqueries: I suggest adding optional field model_overrides: [{model_id, default_view: boolean}]. Backwards compatible if empty.
alicia: That works but watch rollout: older consoles should ignore new field gracefully. Also product wants ability to pin 'preferred' variant for all teammates.
ben: Authz note: pinning should be gated by role. Platform teams might not want every PM to change route-level default model.
sam: Dev question: should routing metadata (preferred_model_id) live in route config service or in console's savedquery? If in route config, it affects live serving routing policies. If in savedquery, it's client-only view preference.
maria: Product explicitly said they want 'console default' not policy change. So savedquery extension seems right, but we should add a clear label: "UI default — does not affect runtime routing".
alicia: Agreed. Also add telemetry labels so we can track adoption: events when users toggle model, open flyout, save query with overrides.
ben: Can we reuse existing telemetry schema? We already have 'route_view.open' and 'model_select.change' events. Add properties: selected_model_id, is_saved_override.
sam: Implementation plan: (1) API: add /routes/:id/telemetry?include_models=true that returns models list; (2) front-end: model pill + flyout; (3) savedquery: optional model_overrides field; (4) telemetry events; (5) small rollout feature flag.
maria: Timeline: UX + API PRs next week; savedquery schema change requires migration plan for older saved queries — default to keep previous single model pin behavior.
alicia: Outstanding questions: do we show cost deltas relative to route default or relative to cheapest variant? Product prefers relative to current default.
ben: I think it's clearer to show both: delta_from_default and delta_from_cheapest (small micro-copy). But ok to start with delta_from_default only.
sam: Also: point of confusion — many routes have A/B routing policies that already pick model per traffic. We should mark when a model is not actually routable for all traffic (label: "may be partial rollout").
maria: Good call. Add a badge with rollout scope: GLOBAL / PARTIAL / CONSOLE-ONLY.
deploy-bot: deploy-notice: staging frontend + telemetry API deployed to staging at 2024-06-12T15:02Z :rocket:
alicia: I'll file a short RFC doc with these decisions and include mocks. Putting a checkbox list in the RFC for savedquery migration, telemetry schema, authz.
ben: Thanks — ping me for API review.
sam: I'll drop the mock in #design after lunch.
maria: Moving to implement — will open the savedquery PR after API lands.
alicia: Great, closing this thread for now. If anything urgent pop into #product or DM. :thumbsup:
